python.datawork.name: Python for Data Work
python.datawork.summary: Python's data ecosystem centers on pandas for tabular data and NumPy for numerical computing.

pandas.name: Pandas DataFrame
pandas.summary: A pandas DataFrame is a two-dimensional labeled data structure resembling a table with named columns and a row index.

numpy.name: NumPy Arrays
numpy.summary: NumPy's ndarray is a homogeneous n-dimensional array enabling efficient vectorized computation.

data_cleaning.name: Data Cleaning
data_cleaning.summary: Data cleaning is the process of fixing errors, inconsistencies, and structural issues in raw data before analysis.

missing_values.name: Missing Values
missing_values.summary: Missing values (NaN in pandas, null in SQL) represent unknown or uncollected data that must be handled before modeling.

visualization.name: Data Visualization
visualization.summary: Visualization translates data into graphics to reveal patterns, trends, and anomalies that numbers alone obscure.

statistics.name: Descriptive Statistics
statistics.summary: Descriptive statistics summarize the central tendency, spread, and shape of a dataset.

probability.name: Probability Basics
probability.summary: Probability quantifies uncertainty, measuring how likely an event is on a scale from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).

distributions.name: Probability Distributions
distributions.summary: A probability distribution assigns probabilities to outcomes of a random variable; key distributions model common data-generating processes.

train_test_split.name: Train/Test Split
train_test_split.summary: Splitting data into training and test sets evaluates how a model generalizes to unseen data.

classification.name: Classification
classification.summary: Classification predicts a discrete class label (spam/not spam, iris species) from input features.

logistic_regression.name: Logistic Regression
logistic_regression.summary: Logistic regression models the probability of a binary outcome as a logistic (sigmoid) function of a linear combination of features.

decision_trees.name: Decision Trees
decision_trees.summary: A decision tree splits data recursively on feature values, creating a flowchart-like model that's easy to interpret.

regression.name: Regression
regression.summary: Regression predicts a continuous numerical outcome (house price, GDP growth) from input features.

linear_regression.name: Linear Regression
linear_regression.summary: Linear regression predicts a continuous target as a weighted sum of features, fit by ordinary least squares (OLS).

clustering.name: Clustering
clustering.summary: Clustering groups similar data points without predefined labels — an unsupervised technique for discovering structure.

kmeans.name: K-Means Clustering
kmeans.summary: K-means partitions $n$ points into $k$ clusters, each represented by its centroid, minimizing within-cluster variance.

feature_engineering.name: Feature Engineering
feature_engineering.summary: Feature engineering transforms raw data into model-friendly inputs, often determining model success more than algorithm choice.

model_evaluation.name: Model Evaluation
model_evaluation.summary: Model evaluation quantifies how well a model performs, using metrics tailored to the problem type and business goal.

accuracy.name: Accuracy
accuracy.summary: Accuracy is the proportion of correct predictions (both true positives and true negatives) out of all predictions.

precision_recall.name: Precision and Recall
precision_recall.summary: Precision measures how trustworthy positive predictions are; recall measures how many actual positives the model captures.

f1_score.name: F1 Score
f1_score.summary: The F1 score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall, balancing both in a single metric.

roc_auc.name: ROC and AUC
roc_auc.summary: The ROC curve plots true positive rate (recall) against false positive rate at every classification threshold; AUC summarizes it.

overfitting.name: Overfitting
overfitting.summary: Overfitting occurs when a model learns the training data too well — including its noise — and generalizes poorly.

underfitting.name: Underfitting
underfitting.summary: Underfitting occurs when a model is too simple to capture the underlying pattern, performing poorly on both training and test data.

cross_validation.name: Cross-Validation
cross_validation.summary: Cross-validation splits data into $k$ folds, training on $k-1$ and validating on the held-out fold, rotating until every fold has been the test set.

leakage.name: Data Leakage
leakage.summary: Data leakage occurs when information from the test set sneaks into the training process, making evaluation overly optimistic.

bias_variance.name: Bias-Variance Tradeoff
bias_variance.summary: Bias-variance decomposition separates a model's error into bias (systematic error from wrong assumptions) and variance (sensitivity to training data).

regularization.name: Regularization
regularization.summary: Regularization adds a penalty to the loss function to discourage overly complex models, reducing overfitting.

ensemble.name: Ensemble Methods
ensemble.summary: Ensemble methods combine multiple models into one prediction, typically reducing variance (bagging) or bias (boosting).

pca.name: Principal Component Analysis
pca.summary: PCA finds orthogonal directions of maximum variance in data, projecting onto a lower-dimensional subspace.

time_series.name: Time Series Analysis
time_series.summary: Time series analysis handles data ordered chronologically, where temporal dependencies matter.

deployment.name: Model Deployment
deployment.summary: Deploying a model means making it available to make predictions on new data in a production environment.

browser_ml.name: Browser and Local ML
browser_ml.summary: Running ML models directly in the browser or on the local machine without a server enables privacy-preserving, low-latency inference.

eda.name: Exploratory Data Analysis
eda.summary: EDA is the initial investigation of a dataset to understand its structure, spot anomalies, and generate hypotheses.

outliers.name: Outlier Detection
outliers.summary: Outliers are data points that deviate significantly from the overall pattern; they may indicate errors, rare events, or genuine extreme behavior.

standardization.name: Feature Scaling
standardization.summary: Feature scaling standardizes the range or distribution of features so that no single feature dominates distance calculations.

dimensionality_reduction.name: Dimensionality Reduction
dimensionality_reduction.summary: Dimensionality reduction transforms high-dimensional data into a lower-dimensional representation while preserving key structure.
